pr_title: tests: kernel: sched: adjust priority preemptible test for acrn_ehl_crb
pr_body:
Make an adjustment on the starting time interval for the test: test_priority_preemptible_wait_prio() to fit the acrn_ehl_crb boards.

There are threads t0, t1, t2, t3, t4 in this test, and the expecting order should be 0,1,2,3. The t1 has higher priority, and t1 should be executed prior to t2. In the falied test we got an order 0,2,1,3, because the t2 already completed but t1 has not start yet, due to the thread spend less time to start (it runs at 1.9G), in this case, the delay interval of each thread starting should be scale.

Fixes #49614.

Signed-off-by: Enjia Mai <enjia.mai@intel.com>

issue_context.title: acrn_ehl_crb: The testcase tests/kernel/sched/schedule_api failed to run.
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
The testcase tests/kernel/sched/schedule_api failed to run on the acrn_ehl_crb.

**To Reproduce**
twister -p acrn_ehl_crb --device-testing --device-serial-pty=$HOME/acrn-env/acrn-test-pty.exp --west-flash=$HOME/acrn-env/acrn_efi.sh -v -T tests/kernel/sched/schedule_api/ -vv

**Logs and console output**
```
ACRN:\>
ACRN:\>vm_console 0
----- Entering VM 0 Shell -----
*** Booting Zephyr OS build zephyr-v3.1.0-4286-gccfe9513ecee  ***
Running TESTSUITE threads_scheduling
===================================================================
START - test_bad_priorities
PASS - test_bad_priorities in 0.001 seconds
...
===================================================================
START - test_sleep_cooperative
PASS - test_sleep_cooperative in 0.561 seconds
===================================================================
START - test_sleep_wakeup_preemptible
PASS - test_sleep_wakeup_preemptible in 0.001 seconds
===================================================================
START - test_slice_perthread
Assertion failed at WEST_TOPDIR/zephyr/tests/kernel/sched/schedule_api/src/test_slice_scheduling.c:159: slice_expired: ((dt - PERTHREAD_SLICE_TICKS) <= TICK_SLOP is false)
slice expired >4 ticks late (dt=357)

PASS - test_slice_reset in 1.801 seconds
===================================================================
```

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

OS: Linux
Toolchain: Zephyr SDK 0.15.0
Commit: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/commit/ccfe9513ecee6dda0525735c96cf0efa1f30d824
comments:
After bisect, I find that this is due to the commit 672d0962c004a5a790d91bad9f4b84a85f43855b
```
672d0962c004a5a790d91bad9f4b84a85f43855b is the first bad commit
commit 672d0962c004a5a790d91bad9f4b84a85f43855b
Author: Andy Ross <andrew.j.ross@intel.com>
Date:   Wed Mar 2 11:36:14 2022 -0800

    tests/kernel/schedule_api: Add TIMESLICE_PER_THREAD case
    
    Simple coverage exerciser for the per-thread timeslice feature.  Added
    as a(nother) new variant of the schedule_api test.
    
    Signed-off-by: Andy Ross <andrew.j.ross@intel.com>

 tests/kernel/sched/schedule_api/src/main.c         |  3 +-
 tests/kernel/sched/schedule_api/src/test_sched.h   |  1 +
 .../sched/schedule_api/src/test_slice_scheduling.c | 71 +++++++++++++++++++++-
 tests/kernel/sched/schedule_api/testcase.yaml      |  6 ++
 4 files changed, 79 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)
```

Still working on it.
@andyross does this one ring any bell? (see the comment above)
acrn_ehl_crb use apic_tsc timer, for acrn, I suspect that CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC=10000 is too high, I set it to 1000, 800, 500, the failed test cases passed.

After bisect, the 
- tests/kernel/sched/schedule_api/kernel.scheduler.multiq_no_timeslicing
- tests/kernel/sched/schedule_api/kernel.scheduler.no_timeslicing
started failed from ec8a3ba7a8ca9de53d9171aaef5dcd856d0b3b66.

And this is a newly added test cases, the failure is order dependent.
- tests/kernel/sched/schedule_api/kernel.scheduler.slice_perthread

The debugging results：
(1) For test_slice_perthread() failed:
After debugging, I found issue happens because at certain point of timing, the hypervisor will have a long delay.
(At about uptime at 106 ms, 632 ms, we will get many cycles late when we call k_cycle_get_32/64().
These points affects some timing sensitive testcases (such as tests/timer/timer_behavior, tests/kernel/smp etc) or even some scheduling tests those measure the time.
We are still not totally clear why the hypervisor will have such a delay at these point. It is most likely not an issue of Zephyr, because the clock cycle read from rdtsc provided by hypervisor.
A suggested workaround solution is to add a 700ms boot delay to avoid these point. We can add CONFIG_BOOT_DELAY=700 for it.

(2) For test_priority_preemptible_wait_prio() failed:
There are threads t0, t1, t2, t3, t4 in this test, and the expecting order should be 0,1,2,3. The t1 has higher priority and waiting for long time, and t1 should be executed prior to t2. In the falied test we got an order 0,2,1,3, because the t2 already completed but t1 has not start yet, due to the thread spend less time to start. (it runs at 1.9G), in this case, the delay interval of each thread starting should be scale.
I think this issue is likely not the problem of zephyr. Lower its priority.

review_comments:
Maybe I am missing something, but I am not yet seeing how a higher board frequency or changing the thread should affect the test results.

I saw in your comments in the issue that in the failing log case, threads were created in the following order:
   T0, T1, T2, T3 (as expected)
And were awoken/entered in the following order:
   T0, T2, T1, T3 (as expected)

However, I do not yet understand how changing the delay times could impact the order in which the threads were removed from the *sync_sema* wait queue.
